Hey there! Summer is our favourite season here in Vancouver. The clouds finally clear off, everyone heads out camping, and every night somebody around a fire points up and asks "what's that bright one?" That's exactly the question Thimbleberry Sky answers. It's our little iPhone app (just the two of us, plus a very opinionated cat) that names whatever star, planet or constellation you aim your phone at, and it keeps working offline out in the backcountry.

We want a short summer push on X. Please run it from Tuesday, July 13, 2027 through Tuesday, July 20, 2027, Pacific time. The goal is simple: as many installs of the iPhone app as possible. Installs are what we count, and nothing else matters to us for this one.

Our posts and landing page do the work: people tap through to https://thimbleberrysky.app/summer and install from there, so there's no app-install campaign or app ID to set up. The app only exists on iPhone (iOS), so Android folks can't install it, and we only offer it in the United States and Canada.

Tracking is in place. X's pixel is on our site, and every install gets reported to X as an event we called "App installed".

Here's the copy from our landing page, word for word:
"Thimbleberry Sky is the stargazing app that names every star, planet and constellation you point your iPhone at, even with zero signal at the campsite. It's free to download, and this summer the full Summer Sky Pack (offline star maps plus a Perseids night guide) is included free until July 31, 2027. Available on iPhone (iOS) only, for stargazers in the United States and Canada."

You have the green light to launch and manage the campaign yourself. No need to check with us before making changes. Please keep an eye on it for the whole run, and when it wraps up, send us a short recap with spend, impressions and link clicks. Clear skies, and thank you!

Total budget: 750.00 USD for everything you launch: every campaign and ad group draws on this one budget. We've approved these 5 posts, all on our account, and only these, so please don't write new ones. Promote whichever you think will work, in as many campaigns and ad groups as you like, and change, pause or stop them as you learn what works:
